observations.content: Bootstrapped Doxa landing-gates infra (kg-guard CI, claude-code-review workflow, kg-save/review/test PreToolUse hooks, attest-review + knowledge-graph-merkle CommonJS scripts) ported from openclaw, adapted for this repo's ESM package.json (.cjs script names) and TS/discord.js/supabase stack.
Second observation to confirm append path still works after saveGraph refactor.

Applied the doxa-browser-extension gate fixes to this repo, which the kit was copied from. (1) 'gh repo view $dir' is an argument error -- gh takes OWNER/REPO, never a filesystem path -- so it always failed and silently disabled the PR-file-list lookups review-gate.sh and test-gate.sh depend on; replaced with repo_slug_of(), which reads the slug from the checkout's origin remote. (2) review-gate.sh OR'd the PR's real head SHA into the local worktree tips, and the loop passes if ANY candidate is attested, so the extra candidate could only ever make the gate MORE permissive -- verified admitting a 'gh pr merge N' on the strength of an unrelated attested local tip. The remote head is now the ONLY candidate when it resolves, with local tips as the offline fallback. (3) where kg-save-gate.sh guarded a check-kg-merge-integrity path whose extension did not match the file this repo ships, the [ -f ] test was permanently false and the PR #343 data-loss guard never ran. All three are the same class: a gate that reports without gating, silently. scripts/check-gate-health.mjs in openclaw is the mechanical detector for the class.

Fourth defect, found by the new medic (openclaw scripts/check-gate-health.mjs) and NOT by the manual pass that fixed the other three: test-gate.sh's test_re was '^(src/.+\\.test\\.(ts|js)|tests/.+)$' in a repo whose only tests are scripts/*.test.cjs and which has no tests/ directory and no colocated src tests. The pattern matched NOTHING against git ls-files, so the gate could never block -- it sat green while gating nothing, for as long as it has existed. Retargeted to the real layout (test_re covers scripts/*.test.cjs; code_re widened from ^src/ to ^(src|scripts)/ so the KG tooling this repo ships is itself gated). Generalisable lesson: a ported gate's PATTERNS are repo-specific state, and copying a kit without re-deriving them against the destination's actual file list produces a gate that is present, wired, executable and completely inert. PATTERN_MATCHES_NOTHING in the medic is the mechanical check for it.

The Discord bot answers @mentions with the same encouragement as /encourage: buildEncourageReply (src/commands/encourage.ts) is shared by both surfaces so the voice and reply shape are identical — plain markdown content with masked scripture links plus one Doxa app button row, which renders the same through interaction.editReply and message.reply. Each surface passes its own caller id (discord:<userId>, keeping the daily quota per-user) and its own UTM medium so installs stay attributable to the surface that earned them. Written 2026-06-26, left uncommitted in the working tree for two months, banked 2026-09-02 in a fleet-wide sweep.

Independent review found two real defects before merge. (1) HIGH: the handler used message.mentions.users.has(botId), the RAW API list, which includes the replied-to author whenever Discord's 'ping author' reply toggle is on — on by default in every client. So replying to one of the bot's own messages with an unrelated follow-up fired a full paid encourage call on that text and spent the user's daily quota, despite the code comment claiming reply pings did not count. Now message.mentions.has(client.user, { ignoreRepliedUser: true, ignoreRoles: true, ignoreEveryone: true }). (2) MEDIUM: the free 'tell me what you are facing' reply sat ABOVE the per-channel cooldown and global token bucket, so N users each inside their own 10s window could flood a channel with canned replies at no budget cost; the channel cooldown and permission check now gate that branch too.

Garth 2026-09-02, on the Discord mention prompt 'Tell me what you are facing and I will encourage you': 'I hate tell me what you are facing. There is no me here. Doxa is not a person.' Doxa never speaks in the first person and never claims agency of its own — no 'I will', no 'me', no persona. An instruction is the right shape: 'Add what you are facing'. First person belongs to the USER, so an example of what a person types keeps its 'I' ('@DoxaBot I am anxious about a decision'). Applies to every surface: Discord, Telegram, MCP, app microcopy, empty states.

review-gate.sh line 101 carried a botched edit: --repo "20 20 12 61 79 80 81 98 701 33 100 204 250 395 398 399 400repo_slug_of "")" instead of --repo "$(repo_slug_of "$dir")". repo_slug_of was defined and never actually called, so for a bare 'gh pr merge <n>' (no --repo flag) the gh lookup always failed, remote_head_sha stayed empty, and the gate fell back to LOCAL worktree tips — silently reopening the exact hole the surrounding comment says it closes: a merge of PR #N passing on the strength of an unrelated attested SHA sitting in some other local worktree. Found 2026-09-02 while proving the stale chore/add-landing-gates branch was superseded. Verified after repair: repo_slug_of resolves The-Doxa-Way/doxa-discord-bot and gh pr view returns a real head SHA.

2026-10-07 GDPR Art. 9 consent gate: /encourage, /weigh, /promise, /scripture and @mentions forward free text to the Doxa MCP (which calls the AI provider and logs request_payload with caller_id discord:<id> in mcp_calls) only after the user presses the 'I agree' button (custom_id art9_consent:v1.0). /doxaway is not gated (no free text). /privacy withdraws and deletes that user's mcp_calls rows. The bot had no datastore and Doxa had no endpoint for it, so consent lives in doxa-app prod table bot_consents (platform discord) reached through the least-privilege Postgres LOGIN role discord_bot via the Supabase pooler (DATABASE_URL, postgres.js, prepare:false); the role can only EXECUTE discord_bot_consent_{status,grant,withdraw} and is denied every table, so no service-role key sits on Fly. DATABASE_URL is required at boot; the URL is in the macOS Keychain (service 'doxa-discord-bot DATABASE_URL'). Routing moved to src/dispatch.ts so tests (node --test via tsconfig.test.json, npm test) drive it with fakes. Store read errors fail closed.

2026-10-08: the Art. 9 consent notice (src/consent.ts) said 'what you send me' and 'our privacy policy' — first person for Doxa. Now 'Before you start: what you send here…' and 'the Doxa privacy policy'. src/dispatch.test.ts fails if any bot consent/withdraw/thanks/error string uses I/me/my/we/us/our (the user's 'I agree' button label excepted).

2026-10-08 review round: final Discord consent notice reads 'Before you start: what you send to DoxaBot can show your religious beliefs' — naming the product (DoxaBot, Doxa) is the impersonal pattern, not 'here' (ambiguous in a channel) and never 'me/we/our'.

Bumped Dockerfile builder+runtime base images from node:20-slim to node:22-slim: Node 20 is EOL and received no fixes for the 2026-10-21 security releases (Brotli decoder RCE, two TLS hostname-check bypasses, dns.resolve NUL-truncation — all HIGH severity). engines field left at >=20 (floor, not pin).

2026-11-06 (The-Doxa-Way-CNS spec the-doxa-way-control-tower F6): this repo's KG becomes CNS source doxa-discord-bot (authority/registry.yaml). Fleet-wide facts are held by the CNS meta-KG or by the other CNS sources (doxa-app, openclaw, doxa-shared), so this repo's copies were removed (federated, they opened conflicts; the Decision ones queue for Garth): KgMergeIntegrityGuard, FleetSecurityBaseline20261103, CanonicalFleetGates, KgGuardRequiredCheckNaming, FleetGates. LandingGatesInfra (two other repos held different facts under that name) was renamed DiscordBotLandingGatesInfra. Rule: kg-save only facts about THIS repo here, under a repo-scoped name. A gate or fleet fact is a kg-save in The-Doxa-Way-CNS; a gate re-render PR here carries no KG change (title it chore(sync): ..., which KG Guard exempts).

TypeScript 7 (bumped 5.9.3->7.0.2, PR #17) ships its compiler as a per-platform optional package @typescript/typescript-<os>-<arch>; the Dockerfile builder stage therefore installs WITHOUT --omit=optional (with it, npm run build fails: 'Unable to resolve @typescript/typescript-linux-x64'). Runtime stage keeps --omit=optional because TS is a devDependency. No CI job builds the image, so a Dockerfile/dep regression is only caught at fly deploy.

The Doxa Discord server's public text (server description, #welcome channel topic, #welcome pinned welcome post) is code-owned in src/server-profile.ts (doxa-brand Hard Rule 15, Garth 2026-11-07): each leads with 'Record and hold prophetic encouragement for decades.' and the description names 'Doxa: Prophetic Encouragement'. On ClientReady (every deploy/restart) the bot runs syncServerProfile: reads each item, writes only what differs, edits its OWN oldest pin in #welcome (or posts and pins a new one), and reports 'missing permission: <Flag>' instead of writing when it lacks ManageGuild / ManageChannels / PinMessages. Log line: [server-profile] {...}. The token never leaves the Fly machine. Guild 1520163816686747648, #welcome 1520163817256910930. Guard: src/server-profile.test.ts.
